title: Gateway Security
description: Implement API keys, JWT validation, and IP whitelisting.

data.text: The API Gateway is the ideal place to enforce security. Centralizing authentication, authorization, and IP filtering at the gateway protects all services.

terms.definition: A token that identifies the calling application.
Verifying the signature and claims of a JSON Web Token.
Allowing only specific IP addresses to access the API.
Both client and server authenticate each other with certificates.

data.text: The gateway can enforce authorization based on roles, scopes, or claims in the JWT. Services can also enforce fine-grained authorization.
IP whitelisting restricts access to specific IP addresses or ranges. Useful for internal APIs and partner integrations.

data.caption: Gateway Security Flow
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    Client[Client] --> GW[API Gateway]
    GW --> Auth{Authenticate}
    Auth -->|API Key Valid| Authz{Authorize}
    Auth -->|JWT Valid| Authz
    Auth -->|Invalid| Reject401[401 Unauthorized]
    Authz -->|Allowed| Route[Route to Service]
    Authz -->|Denied| Reject403[403 Forbidden]
    Route --> Svc[Service]

data.title: JWT Validation Middleware
data.content: Validating JWT tokens at the gateway.

data.title: Exercise: Secure a Gateway
data.description: Implement security at the API Gateway.
steps: Add rate limiting per API key
data.expectedOutcome: A secured gateway with auth and rate limiting

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use IP whitelisting for internal APIs
data.takeaway: Gateway security protects all services with centralized enforcement.
